# One split writes `$residual$` and another states `took_the_residual`.
#
# The two ways of declaring the difference are equivalent, so writing one of
# each in the same transaction claims it twice. The token resolves on the gain
# line, and the bank charge beside it states the key, and both would count.
#
# Both are expenses or income, so neither the account nor the arithmetic tells
# them apart: that is exactly the case the token and the key exist to settle,
# and a file cannot settle it two ways at once.
#
# Refused for the reason two `$residual$` splits are refused: a transaction has
# one exchange difference, and nothing decides which of two claims is it.
#
# `{usd_basis}` is the guid of the purchase's cost basis, read from
# `fx-balances` after the first import.
2026-06-01 open Expenses
	type: "Expense"
	placeholder: #True
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-06-01 open Expenses:Bank Charges
	type: "Expense"
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

2026-06-01 * "Sell every dollar at 1.40, less a bank charge"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank -1000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-1300.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{usd_basis}"
	Assets:CAD Bank 1395.00 CAD
	Expenses:Bank Charges 5.00 CAD
		took_the_residual: "true"
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
